text.en: A steel spoon left in hot tea soon becomes hot at the other end. A fire warms us even from a distance. Heat travels in three ways.

In conduction, heat travels through a solid from the hot part to the cooler part without the material moving. Metals are good conductors. Wood, plastic and air are poor conductors, called insulators.
In convection, heat is carried by the movement of a liquid or gas. Hot water rises and cooler water sinks, which sets up a circulation. This is why a room heater warms a room: warm air rises.
Radiation is heat travelling as waves, with no material needed. The warmth of the Sun reaches Earth through empty space. Dark objects absorb more radiation than light ones, so we wear light clothes in summer.
During the day land heats faster than the sea, so warm air rises over land and cool air from the sea blows in: a sea breeze. At night the reverse happens: a land breeze. Woollen clothes trap air, which is a poor conductor, and keep us warm in winter.

problem.en: Why do we use a wooden handle on a frying pan?

text.en: Metal conducts heat to the hand.
Wood is a poor conductor so the handle stays cool.

prompt.en: Explain how the Sun's heat reaches us.

requiredIdeas.en: It travels by radiation through space.

points.en: Conduction in solids, convection in fluids, radiation by waves.
Sea and land breezes come from uneven heating.
